articles.body: PUNE: In an attempt to evade traffic police, an SUV driver in Baramati tried to mow down a constable and drove nearly 50 feet with him clinging to the vehicle's bonnet before speeding away.The Pune rural police, however, tracked down the driver in Satara district and arrested him within four hours from Phaltan in Satara district. The incident happened at Samyak Chowk in Baramati on Wednesday around 5pm.The constable sustained severe injuries to his left arm and leg in the incident. TThe SUV driver Dheeraj Shedge, 25, of Rajale village in Phaltan taluka in Satara district has been charged under sections 109 (murder) attempt, 132 (Assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty), 121 (voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty) and 221 (obstructing public servant in the discharge of public functions) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police sub-inspector Sarjerao Pujari of the Baramati City police told TOI that the police costable Dattatreya Bhosale, 47, was manning the traffic at Samyak Chowk in Baramati on Wednesday evening.He noticed a sports utility vehicle (SUV) with a fancy number plate and tinted glass. He told the driver to stop and took out his e-challan machine to photograph the vehicle and issue a challan."Bhosale realised that the driver was planning to escape. So he stood in front of the SUV and instructed him to stop," Pujari said.The officer said that the driver was moving slowly towards the constable. When the vehicle reached the constable, the driver suddenly increased speed, attempting to mow him down."Bhosale held the bonnet of the SUV. The driver however did not slowed down and drove at least 50feet with constable clinging to bonnet," the officer said.Pujari said that Bhosale fell on the road and the accused drove away from there at at high-speed. "Bhosale sustained injuries to his left arm and leg. We shifted him to a hospital," Pujari said.The officer said that with the help of the registration number of the SUV, the police traced it at Rajale village and took Shedge into custody. articles.title: Hundreds of flights canceled on Thanksgiving Day as storms hit and  question swirl over Iowa detonation: Morning Rundown
articles.summary: Bad weather postpones the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade for the first-time ever.
articles.body: Bad weather postpones the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade for the first-time ever. The questions lingering after the Iowa detonation. And, the holiday tradition of deciding to run for president. Here’s what to know today. Severe Thanksgiving weather forces Macy’s parade to reschedule The 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed, as strong winds are expected to sweep through New York City today. The parade is now scheduled to kick off at 8:30 a.m. ET Saturday. NBC will instead air last year’s parade today at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones. This is Morning Rundown, a weekday newsletter to start your day. Sign up here to get it in your inbox. Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a news conference yesterday that New Yorkers will see a heavy storm with forecast sustained winds between 30 and 40 mph and possible gusts as high as 65 mph. City regulations mandate balloons can’t fly if sustained winds exceed 23 mph. The parade has only been cancelled three times, in 1942, 1943 and 1944 — not for bad weather but because materials for the giant balloons were needed for the World War II effort. Balloons were last grounded in 1971 due to fierce winds and rain. Here’s what to know about the Thanksgiving parade’s postponement. The same storm system forcing the parade date move is also expected to bring heavy rain and major coastal flooding along other parts of the East Coast, as well as the Southeast, with 1 to 4 inches of rain expected across the mid-Atlantic and 1 to 2 inches in southern New England. More than 300 flights from, to or within the U.S. have already been canceled so far today. Yesterday more than 150 were canceled and 6,000 flights were delayed. In the Pacific Northwest, storms are expected to bring rain and mountain snow to Washington and Oregon, and high tides are expected to continue hitting the West Coast. Video captured yesterday showed the moment extreme king tides destroyed part of a pier in Pacifica, California. Separately, a FedEx airplane overshot a runway at Miami International Airport last night, forcing all but one of the four runways to temporarily close, according to officials. There were no reports of injuries after the incident at about 8:40 p.m., the airport reported. Early this morning, the Federal Aviation Administration was reporting hourslong flight delays. Follow our live blog for the latest Thanksgiving weather and travel updates. Related coverage: For subscribers: Take a look back at 100 years of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, a holiday spectacle as American as pumpkin pie. Researchers and locals ask what comes next after Iowa blast Federal officials have repeatedly said the Army’s detonation of lead azide in Iowa produced a minimal plume of lead dust. Locals and independent researchers aren’t entirely reassured. Some who reside closest to where the blast took place said they were unsure when it will be safe to return. Sean Byers, who lives across the street from the plant, said he believes “a lot of people in general are downplaying the potential long-term effects of what may be to come simply because they may have perceived the lead plume as less boisterous” than some had feared. While the EPA said that initial data did not detect lead in the atmosphere, outside experts said it will take days to begin to understand whether there are hotspots that require cleanup. The questions lingering in the detonation’s aftermath. What do Thanksgiving feasts have to do with the 2028 election? Many important conversations will happen around dinner tables across the nation this Thanksgiving. Only a few select people, however, will seriously pose the question of whether they should run for president. It’s once again time for a long-standing holiday tradition in American politics — when potential candidates tell reporters that they couldn’t possibly answer questions about a potential presidential campaign right now. That, they say every four years, is because they plan to take the question to their holiday table to discuss it with their loved ones. The holidays are a prime time for these discussions, said former Wisconsin Gov. Scott Walker, who ran unsuccessfully for the Republican nomination in 2016. It’s just about the only time that a politician isn’t being “pulled in multiple directions,” he said, and can spend significant time in one place with the people whose counsel they rely on — not to mention the people whose lives could be upended by the choice. The notable politicians who mulled the big decision over the holidays. Problems with the military’s healthcare system are infuriating patients After Amber Fake learned she had terminal lung cancer, she clung to every moment she could spend with her family. But since her diagnosis two years ago, she says she has also spent far too many hours battling against her Tricare healthcare plan for wrongly refusing to cover medical bills that totaled hundreds of thousands of dollars, leaving her on the hook. Tricare, a health benefits program for more than 9 million service members, retirees and their families, is plagued by bureaucratic snafus, an NBC News investigation found. From incorrect explanations of benefits to unexpected hospital bills, more than 100 military families said that their healthcare or finances have suffered since a disastrous government contract change. For some, like Fake, the only way to get anything resolved was to spend hours on the phone. “I shouldn’t have to do all this when I’m trying to just fight for my life,” she said. Read the full story here. NBC Selected: Get a head start on Black Friday shopping The best way to recover from Thanksgiving dinner? By taking advantage of all the early Black Friday deals that are happening right now. Our team of shopping experts rounded up the best early deals to shop at Amazon, Home Depot, Walmart and more. Plus, these are the products our editors always buy on Black Friday (and some are already deeply discounted). Sign up to The Selection newsletter for hands-on product reviews, expert shopping tips and a look at the best deals and sales each week. Read All About It How are you affording the holidays? The Pittsburgh Steelers released quarterback Aaron Rodgers after he called coach Mike McCarthy “unhealthy” and accused him of sleeping through meetings. More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in Ukraine, according to a new estimate based on leaked data, shedding light on the staggering cost of the war approaching its fifth year. A federal judge has temporarily blocked the FCC from moving forward with its early review of ABC’s broadcast-station licenses, which the media company called an attack on free speech by the Trump administration. More American tech startups are ditching Silicon Valley for Shenzhen, the Chinese metropolis thrust into the spotlight during last week’s Trump-Xi-Putin summit. Here’s why. articles.title: At least 9 injured by large explosion and fire at major oil facility in Bangkok
articles.summary: An explosion and fire at a major oil facility in the Thai capital on Thursday injured at least nine people and forced nearby residents to briefly evacuate, authorities said.
articles.body: An explosion and fire at a major oil facility in the Thai capital on Thursday injured at least nine people and forced nearby residents to briefly evacuate, authorities said. Most of the injured suffered burns and three people were in critical condition, according to Erawan Medical Center in Bangkok. Video posted on social media showed thick black smoke rising from the site in an eastern neighborhood of Bangkok. A mobile phone alert sent to residents said the incident happened around 3 p.m. and advised people to avoid the area. The city authority reported less than an hour later that the ensuing fire was put out. Officials later said nearby residents can return home, but advised those living in a 5-kilometer (3-mile) radius of the facility to be cautious of air pollution. The Pollution Control Department said it sent officials to assess air and water quality in the surrounding area. Bangchak Corp., which owns the refining and storage facility, confirmed the fire in a Facebook post and said that the cause was still being investigated. The company also said it has halted all production operations. Energy Minister Akanat Promphan said the fire appeared to start at one of the refinery units, which is about 100 meters (330 feet) away from the oil storage. He said he would inspect the site to ensure there’s no further risk. “If we’re not a hundred percent certain that the oil storage is safe, we won’t allow them to resume operations,” he said. Akanat said Thailand’s oil supply should not be affected, as there are five other refineries in the country and this facility is not among the biggest. The refinery, with a listed capacity of 120,000 barrels a day, is the fifth biggest in Thailand and the only one situated in an urban area. An explosion and fire at the refinery in July 2012 caused damage in a nearby residential neighborhood and it took two weeks to repair the facility.

articles.title: ‘Symbolic’: Why did UK sanction Yemen’s Houthis amid attacks on Saudi?
articles.summary: UK sanctions Iran-backed group and its leaders, accusing them of undermining stability in the Middle East.
articles.body:
London, United Kingdom – The United Kingdom has slapped sanctions on Yemen’s Houthis and four of their senior leaders after accusing the Iran-backed group of renewed “aggression” inside Yemen and attacks targeting civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

The Houthis have escalated attacks on Saudi Arabia, targeting the financial district in Riyadh this week, as they engage in a civil war with Yemen’s internationally recognised government.

Fighting has escalated since July as a 2022 United Nations-brokered ceasefire collapsed. Since then, the Houthis have captured the Red Sea port of Mocha and the island of Mayyun, extending control over the Red Sea in a setback to the Saudi-backed government.

The war erupted after the Houthis captured the capital, Sanaa, in late 2014, forcing President Abd Rabbu Mansour Hadi to flee. Saudi Arabia intervened in support of the Hadi government as it saw the Iran-backed group’s rise in neighbouring Yemen as a security threat.

The UK government announced its sanctions on Tuesday, accusing the Houthis of undermining peace and security in Yemen and the region. It froze assets and placed travel bans on the group and its leaders, including Interior Minister Abdulkarim Amir al-Din Hussein al-Houthi and Security and Intelligence chief Abdul Hakim Hashem Ali al-Khaiwani.

Chief prosecutor Sarim al-Din Mufadal, who has been accused of perpetrating “sexual violence, including rape and torture”, also faces an asset freeze and travel ban.

“The Houthis’ renewed aggression targeting our partners and innocent civilians is unacceptable, and they must be held to account,” said UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who linked the sanctions to attacks on shipping in the Bab al-Mandeb strait in the Red Sea, one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world.

“Today’s measures send a clear message to the Houthis – we will always act in support of British values and interests,” he said in a statement.

The British move comes nearly a month after it decided to deploy fighter jets to defend Saudi Arabia, a close ally going back decades that has increasingly come under missile and drone attacks in recent weeks.

Britain also sent Tornado fighters to Saudi Arabia in the wake of the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait in 1990, according to the Royal Air Force Museum.

The Houthis have also targeted oil installations and a major pipeline that helped Saudi Arabia export its oil while Iran essentially blocked the Strait of Hormuz, a global oil chokepoint. Tehran said it has blocked the vital waterway, through which most of the Gulf oil and natural gas passes, in response to the US-Israel war on Iran.

The UK has naval and logistics bases in the neighbouring Gulf nations of Bahrain and Oman. In May, it agreed a free trade deal with the six Gulf Cooperation Council states.

Thomas Juneau, an associate fellow with Chatham House’s Middle East and North Africa Programme, said the sanctions were imposed during a diplomatic push by Riyadh.

“Saudi Arabia has been asking other countries to list the Houthis as a terrorist entity, to turn the screw on the Houthis and to help in its campaign against the group,” he told Al Jazeera.

The sanctions, Ahmed Nagi from the International Crisis Group (ICG) said, are “intended to send a political message about where the UK stands on the current escalation and the Houthi actions”.

In January 2024, the UK and the United States jointly sanctioned four Houthi figures, including the group’s defence minister and naval commander, over attacks on Red Sea shipping, and a month later, a second package targeted the Quds Force, the overseas unit of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

The same month, the UK joined the US in carrying out air strikes on Houthi positions over attacks on ships in the Red Sea, which had disrupted maritime trade. The Houthis had imposed a ban on ships linked to Israel from passing through the waterway in response to Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

The Houthis are already under a UN arms embargo, and London is now “going further”, Nagi, who is a senior Yemen analyst at the ICG, said.

This month, the UN Security Council renewed its Yemen sanctions regime until November 2027 through a UK-led resolution.

Raiman al-Hamdani, a Yemeni researcher and analyst, said the UK, as the Security Council’s lead on Yemen, had helped shape that regime and “this latest step continues a longstanding policy rather than breaking from it.”

But Nagi called the UK move “largely symbolic”.

“The four Houthi leaders targeted by the sanctions are unlikely to travel to the UK or hold assets there, so the practical impact will probably be limited.”

Al-Hamdani said the group’s income comes “largely from the black market, smuggling, taxation of local businesses and control of ports and customs, none of which a UK asset freeze touches”.

“The missile and drone programme hasn’t slowed despite years of UN, US, EU and UK listings,” he added.

Juneau from Chatham House agreed the sanctions would not change Houthi behaviour soon but said that while sanctions by individual countries other than the US have little effect alone, they can matter collectively, which is why Saudi Arabia is pressing as many countries as possible to act.

He also pointed to the Houthis’ growing influence in the Red Sea, which has concerned Saudi Arabia as well as its Western allies.

The British foreign secretary on Tuesday pointed out how Houthi actions in the Red Sea were “driving up the cost of living for the British people” and “undermining the stability of the Middle East”.

Analysts pointed out that the UK government statement is silent on the other parties to the war – the Yemeni government forces and Saudi Arabia – even as it said the Houthis’ “reckless aggression is responsible for this conflict”.

Nagi said the omission reflected how London sees the war.

“From London’s perspective, the Houthis are the ones attacking Saudi Arabia and escalating the conflict, rather than the other way around,” he said.

Juneau was blunter. “Sanctions are always political. You sanction your opponents. You don’t sanction your partners or friends,” he said.

Niku Jafarnia, a Yemen researcher at Human Rights Watch, expressed concerns that the sanctions would impact aid organisations engaged in humanitarian work in Houthi-held areas.

“As Yemen relies heavily on imports, curbs affecting commercial goods could also push up food prices,” she told Al Jazeera.

“The sanctions really can have quite devastating impacts for the populations living in territories under Houthi control, even if that’s not what the UK intends by the sanctions,” she warned.

This is the case even though the UK’s sanctions already include a humanitarian exception covering aid and other activities that meet basic human needs, she said.

Moreover, the UK has not proscribed the Houthis under “antiterrorism” laws despite its other Western allies – the US, Canada and Australia – designating the Iran-backed group as a “terrorist” organisation.

Juneau called the aid agencies’ fear that proscription could hamper humanitarian deliveries “a valid concern” although some people argued the Houthis’ diversion of aid has already made such work extremely difficult.

The Houthis have repeatedly denied that they have diverted humanitarian aid.

Al-Hamdani said sanctions have not forced the Houthis to change their tactics. They do not “appear to respond to human rights criticism or listings”, he said, adding that the group “tends to treat detainees and abuses as bargaining chips to strengthen its negotiating position and demands”.

Rather, he said, sanctions “risk deepening polarisation and closing off the political settlement the war needs”.

articles.title: Aurigny prioritises lifeline route to Alderney over winter months
articles.summary: Aurigny puts focus on Alderney service during January and December after 'unacceptable' disruption.
articles.body:
Aurigny has announced it will be prioritising the Guernsey to Alderney route for Alderney residents after only 85% of flights on the route were completed as scheduled from January to September.

The airline said it would reduce Alderney to Southampton flights in order to prioritise the "lifeline route" between Alderney and Guernsey in December and January.

The changes follow what the airline called "a period of unacceptable levels of disruption".

It said it would run four return flights a day on the Alderney-Guernsey route and would run one direct Alderney-Southampton return flight on Mondays and Fridays.

The airline said on other days passengers could travel between Alderney and Southampton via Guernsey and it would offer refunds and re-routing for affected passengers.

It said it would prioritise rebooking for travellers with healthcare appointments or connections and those travelling over the festive period.

Aurigny's chief executive Nico Bezuidenhout said: "Weather, including periods of fog and strong crosswinds earlier in the year, caused around half of this year's cancellations, and some of that disruption is beyond any operator's control."

But he added crew shortages were "not acceptable" and the company was pressing Skybus , which operates the service to Alderney, for a lasting solution. Skybus has been contacted for comment.

The airline has previously apologised "unreservedly" for disruption caused by unprecedented levels of staff sickness.

Bezuidenhout said the arrival of a dedicated Twin Otter aircraft was an "important step".

He added: "We are putting additional aircraft and crew arrangements in place."

Reacting to the announcement, Alderney States member Alex Snowdon said: "We can't go on having sort of crisis mode after crisis mode, which I think we have warned about to some degree already, but this seems to be a next level at the moment."

He added the Alderney to Southampton route was worth more than £1.8m to the Alderney economy.

Fellow States member Edward Hill said: "It has reached a point where this should really never have happened and it is disappointing.

"The only positive about it is that there will actually be four flights a day between Alderney and Guernsey which is actually one flight more than there was before so there's always a little light in a rather dark cloud."

articles.title: Huge plume of black smoke seen from space after Houthis claim strike on Saudi’s biggest oil refinery
articles.summary: Satellite imagery taken Wednesday showed a huge plume of black smoke rising from Saudi Arabia’s coastal Ras Tanura peninsula after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed to have attacked the kingdom’s biggest oil refinery.
articles.body: Satellite imagery taken Wednesday showed a huge plume of black smoke rising from Saudi Arabia’s coastal Ras Tanura peninsula after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed to have attacked the kingdom’s biggest oil refinery. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the strikes “were accurate and direct” and caused a fire at the Ras Tanura facility, part of one of the world’s largest crude oil export terminals. A shipping source told CNN Thursday that oil loadings at the terminal were suspended after the attack. It’s unclear whether they have resumed. The Houthis have targeted infrastructure in Saudi Arabia repeatedly in recent weeks – including an attack on the capital Riyadh’s financial district – as the fallout from the US-Iran war drags on. Riyadh’s international airport was also hit several times last month, killing more than a dozen people. On Wednesday, the Saudi-led coalition battling the Houthi rebels said it intercepted and destroyed four drones in Ras Tanura in the kingdom’s eastern province. The interception resulted in falling debris, but no injuries were reported, the Coalition Forces spokesman Major General Turki Al-Malki said, citing an initial assessment. Ras Tanura, which has been targeted previously during the conflict, has a refining capacity of 550,000 barrels per day and is part of a broader coastal complex that housed the kingdom’s main export terminal before the US-Iran war began in late February. CNN has approached Saudi state-owned oil giant Aramco for comment. Strikes reported in Yemen Separately on Wednesday, the Saudi-led coalition said it had attacked “operational capabilities” in the Houthi-controlled Hodeidah port and “destroyed a number of targets” in Saada and Amran governorates, as tit-for-tat strikes between the two sides escalate. Houthi-affiliated al-Masirah TV reported that Saudi-led forces launched airstrikes on Hodeidah city, including an attack at the Hodeidah International Airport. The port at Hodeidah serves as a key supply route for the Houthis. Several Saudi airstrikes were reported on Thursday, including on the Yemeni capital Sanaa, according to al-Masirah TV. CNN has not been able to independently verify the attacks. Fighting between the Houthi group and the Saudi-led coalition reignited in July after years of relative calm brought about by a 2022 UN-brokered ceasefire. Clashes intensified in recent months after the militant group made an advance toward the critical Bab el-Mandeb Strait in September, threatening a new front in the Iran war. In their Wednesday statement, the Houthis also claimed responsibility for a strike on the King Abdullah Economic City in Riyadh that Saudi authorities said wounded 11 people. It was the third such attack this month in the Saudi capital. In response to the Riyadh attack, the Saudi-led coalition said the “deliberate targeting of civilians and civilian objects by the Houthi terrorist militia will be met with a firm response.” An eyewitness in Riyadh told CNN the targeted building, the tallest in the Saudi capital, was the headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s trillion-dollar sovereign wealth fund, the Public Investment Fund (PIF). The skyscraper was also struck earlier this month in a missile attack.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen set up for another shootout as Chiefs face Bills on Thanksgiving
articles.summary: The Chiefs and Bills meet on Thanksgiving Day with Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen poised for an NFL shootout; the series is tied 5-5 since 2020.
articles.body: I don’t know if you know this or not, but we are at the main course of your Thanksgiving Day with this game. Sure, you could’ve finished and might be in a food coma by the time this game kicks off, but the NFL has done a great job of giving us one game that we absolutely cannot miss late in the day. Any time the Chiefs and the Bills take each other on, it is must-see television, and that’s precisely what we get this week. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The Kansas City Chiefs are one of the best teams in football again. They are coming off yet another win – a 34-7 drubbing of the Arizona Cardinals. I do think it is fair to ask if the Chiefs are actually good, or just taking advantage of an easy schedule. Their eight wins have been over Denver, Indianapolis, Miami, Las Vegas, Los Angeles (Chargers), New York (Jets), Atlanta, and Arizona. Outside of Denver, whom they played at home and in the first week of the season, there isn’t one quality win in that group. In fact, none of those teams have winning records. So, are the Chiefs actually good? Maybe. Patrick Mahomes has played much more like Patrick Mahomes in the past two games, throwing for 672 yards over the two games and eight touchdowns. We know he doesn’t really have a deep receiving corps, but he is making it work. I’ve harped about this for years, but Rashee Rice, Josh Downs, and Xavier Worthy are the options, and I don’t think any of them would be a true No. 1 on almost any other team. Travis Kelce sporadically looks good, but you can’t really count on it. Kenneth Walker III is a difference-maker at running back, but he has been out the past two weeks, and they really need him to give the Bills defense something different to worry about. The Buffalo Bills are still one of the best teams in football, and they still have their Superman, Josh Allen. articles.title: Parents of potential first Gen Z saint share daughter's powerful final message of hope
articles.summary: Maria Middleton's parents recall her words after a terminal brain tumor diagnosis as bishops advance her cause to become the first Gen Z saint.
articles.body: The parents of a Doylestown, Pennsylvania, teenager who could become the Catholic Church's first Gen Z saint are sharing their daughter's powerful message of hope, recalling how she remained steadfast in her faith while braving a terminal brain tumor diagnosis. "I will not despair. I will choose hope," Maria Middleton told her parents just two weeks after her diagnosis. Her father, Brian Middleton, recounted the conversation Tuesday on "The Story with Martha MacCallum." Brian, along with his wife, Susan, joined the show to reflect on their daughter's legacy and the movement to canonize her as a saint. GEN Z FLOCKING TO CATHOLIC CHURCHES IN NYC FOR YOUTH GROUPS, SOCIAL EVENTS AMID CONVERSION BOOM "Maria made a decision that she wasn't going to cling to life, that she was going to spend it in self-transcendent service to others," Brian said, recalling his daughter's determination to not let her diagnosis define her remaining time. "Two weeks after she was diagnosed, we asked her how she was doing. And she said, 'Mom and Dad, regardless of the circumstances of my life, my mission and purpose remain the same, and it's to know, love and serve God... my emotions will rise and fall, but my faith is not an emotion. It's a commitment and I will not despair. I will choose hope,'" he added. "Her faith was so well integrated into her life that her decisions were always based on what was good, what was true, what was beautiful," Susan chimed in. "That's how Maria navigated through life, always going back and saying to herself, and we found this in her journal... 'Only what God thinks matters.'" FULTON SHEEN BECAME A TV SENSATION PREACHING FAITH, MORALITY AND WARNINGS MICHAEL KNOWLES SAYS STILL RESONATE Maria died in 2020 at just 18 years old, approximately 20 months after being diagnosed with an inoperable brain tumor. Her commitment to faith and serving others has since drawn widespread attention, prompting Catholic leaders to take a preliminary step toward her possible canonization. On Nov. 17, the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops voted to advance Middleton's cause for canonization, marking an early step in a process that could eventually see her recognized as the Catholic Church's first Gen Z saint. The move comes a little over one year after Pope Leo canonized the first millennial saint, St. Carlo Acutis. For her parents, the growing movement to recognize Maria as a saint reflects the lasting impact of her message, which they say continues to resonate with people around the world. "In this world of despair, she's become a patroness of hope because of the way that she lived her life. In this world with anxiety, suicide, and depression, Maria made a decision that she was going to live out her life on a daily basis. She chose gratitude over anger," Brian said. "But the thing that's undeniable is the impact that Maria has had on so many lives around the world... in this age of despair, she's a light of hope."

articles.title: Bihar open school board probe detects forged certificates, lodges FIR
articles.summary: Bihar Board of Open Schooling (BBOSE) files FIR in Patna after internal probe finds fake certificates; verification to move to DigiLocker and SDC security.
articles.body: Patna: Bihar Board of Open Schooling and Examination (BOSE) lodged an FIR at Jakkanpur police station in Patna on Thursday after several certificates allegedly issued by the board were found to be fake during an internal inquiry. The inquiry has also indicated the possible involvement of some BBOSE and National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) employees and others in the alleged forgery.The irregularities came to light during an internal review initiated by BBOSE chief executive officer (CEO) Sajjan R after he took charge around a month ago. After noticing discrepancies during certificate verification, he constituted a three-member committee to probe the matter. Based on its findings, the board identified suspected cases of forged certificates and possible involvement of individuals in their preparation and verification.According to the FIR, the NIOS regional office had sent several certificates to BBOSE through separate letters for verification. During scrutiny, most of them were found to be fake. The inquiry also found that some verification letters issued by BBOSE to NIOS were also allegedly forged.The departmental inquiry indicated the possible involvement of certain learners and employees of the two institutions in the alleged fraud. Following the findings, a senior executive officer of BBOSE’s examination and evaluation department lodged the complaint, seeking legal action against those found responsible.Meanwhile, the board has decided to strengthen its certificate verification and document security systems to prevent such incidents. Sajjan said certificates would henceforth be verified through DigiLocker, while confidential board documents would be stored on the State Data Centre (SDC) server with password protection.He added that the board would introduce a standard operating procedure (SOP) to streamline certificate verification and strengthen safeguards against document forgery.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news. articles.title: French film star Gerard Depardieu to stand trial for rape, lawyer says
articles.summary: Film star Gerard ​Depardieu, one of the leading faces of French cinema, will face trial on charges of raping actress Charlotte Arnould, his lawyer said.
articles.body: Film star Gerard ​Depardieu, one of the leading faces of French cinema, will face trial on charges of raping actress Charlotte Arnould ⁠in 2018, his lawyer David-Olivier Kaminski said on Thursday. Arnould first accused Depardieu of rape in 2018, saying the assaults occurred in his Paris home ⁠on two separate ​occasions when ⁠she was in her early 20s. Depardieu, 77, has denied wrongdoing in ⁠the case, and his legal team last ​year ⁠appealed prosecutors’ decision for ‌the case to be tried. Depardieu - a towering figure in French cinema, who starred in more ‌than 200 films over ‌five decades, including “Green Card,” “The Last Metro” and “Cyrano de Bergerac” — has become one of the most ⁠high-profile faces of France’s slow-burn reckoning with sexual abuse by some of its most powerful men. Earlier this month, Depardieu withdrew his appeal against a separate 2025 conviction for sexual assault, accepting his guilt and apologizing to ‌his victims. The rape trial poses a ​much more serious threat to Depardieu, ‌who could face ⁠15-20 years in jail if he ⁠is convicted. Earlier this month, British comedian Russell Brand was jailed for ‌10-and-a-half years ​after he was ‌convicted of raping one woman ​and sexually assaulting three others.
